problem_fragment: Ongoing sessions contain forecast-time state information
what_is_already_solved: Elapsed occupation time and live connector state improve remaining-duration prediction.
unresolved_detail: The output is waiting/availability rather than future station power, and future arrivals are not modeled jointly.
implication_for_direction: An active-session power branch is justified, but remaining-duration prediction alone is already occupied.

problem_fragment: Partial traces reveal the remainder of a DC fast-charging curve
what_is_already_solved: A large-scale model can update individual power-profile and duration forecasts from one or a few observed power/SOC points.
unresolved_detail: It does not aggregate simultaneous active sessions with stochastic future arrivals into a station forecast.
implication_for_direction: Use partial-trajectory conditioning for the active-session component; do not claim individual curve prediction as new.

problem_fragment: Future arrivals, duration and power are event-driven
what_is_already_solved: Compound Poisson/Cox models jointly model event arrivals, duration and power and can generate short-term station profiles.
unresolved_detail: The model is calibrated from historical events and does not condition the future load on the exact partially observed sessions active at forecast issue time.
implication_for_direction: Use an event/mark model for the future-arrival component; changing Poisson to a neural point process is not sufficient novelty.

problem_fragment: Direct and bottom-up probabilistic EV-load baselines exist
what_is_already_solved: Direct quantile models, session bottom-up mixtures and adaptive conformal prediction are evaluated across horizons.
unresolved_detail: Bottom-up load reconstruction assumes constant charging power and the real-time correction is not a state decomposition of active versus future sessions.
implication_for_direction: The primary candidate must outperform both direct probabilistic and bottom-up session baselines and explicitly use legal live state.

problem_fragment: Occupancy and load can be jointly predicted
what_is_already_solved: Mixed occupancy-load predictors have been built at individual-charger level for a 24 h horizon.
unresolved_detail: They are deterministic and do not quantify source-specific uncertainty or exploit partial active-session power traces.
implication_for_direction: Joint occupancy is a baseline, not the contribution; the gap is source-resolved rolling probabilistic aggregation.

problem_fragment: Whole-curve accuracy can hide operational peak failure
what_is_already_solved: A multistep LSTM study reports large peak-magnitude and peak-time deviations at several charging-site types.
unresolved_detail: Peak timing/intensity are evaluated after the fact rather than learned as a structured joint target.
implication_for_direction: Peak location, magnitude and ramp errors should be first-class outputs/metrics and can support a lower-risk backup direction.

problem_fragment: Peak timing is not equivalent to profile magnitude accuracy
what_is_already_solved: A dedicated forecasting challenge shows few studies target peak timing and formalizes timing/shape tracks.
unresolved_detail: The method is general electricity forecasting rather than EV charging.
implication_for_direction: An EV peak paper must exploit charging-event structure and operational consequences, not only import a generic loss.

problem_fragment: Constant/linear session curves can distort station peaks
what_is_already_solved: Measurement-based comparisons show linear profile models can create large modelling errors, especially with control.
unresolved_detail: The study assesses profile assumptions but does not learn latent high-resolution curves from weak session labels.
implication_for_direction: Weak-label, multi-fidelity curve reconstruction is a concrete high-value gap with a strict identifiability gate.

problem_fragment: Requested, setpoint and realized power are distinct
what_is_already_solved: The EPFL dataset exposes P, Pset, Preq, SOC and control flags at one-minute resolution.
unresolved_detail: It is small and single-site, and realized power is affected by station power sharing.
implication_for_direction: Use it to validate active-session/control-aware models and to expose label endogeneity, not as the sole forecasting benchmark.

problem_fragment: A large session dataset includes measured charging current and pilot signals
what_is_already_solved: ACN-Data provides connection/disconnection, delivered energy, current and pilot time series.
unresolved_detail: The network is adaptively controlled; observed power is not automatically an uncontrolled demand label.
implication_for_direction: Any model using ACN must preserve pilot/control fields and distinguish required energy from executed power.

problem_fragment: Managed charging changes the observed load-generating process
what_is_already_solved: A large field experiment reports substantial peak-hour load shifting under AI-managed charging.
unresolved_detail: The working paper does not provide a directly reusable station-level forecasting dataset.
implication_for_direction: Control-policy endogeneity is a legitimate second-stage problem: forecast latent charging need and policy-conditioned executed power separately.

problem_fragment: Observed transactions can be censored by charger supply
what_is_already_solved: Censored regression and graph models estimate latent demand omitted by occupied stations and competitors.
unresolved_detail: Multiple mechanisms such as faults, queue abandonment and policy control remain difficult to identify from public logs.
implication_for_direction: Keep latent-demand forecasting as a data-gated route; do not present censoring awareness alone as new.

problem_fragment: Traffic and queue mechanisms already map arrivals to load distributions
what_is_already_solved: A probabilistic queue model converts traffic forecasts and arrival rates into charging-load uncertainty under service limits.
unresolved_detail: It is not a live station-state decomposition using partially observed active charging curves.
implication_for_direction: Queue/event models are strong baselines for the future-arrival branch.

problem_fragment: Forecast-time legality and local ramps matter
what_is_already_solved: A recent framework explicitly restricts inputs to information available at issue time and targets local ramps/peaks.
unresolved_detail: Its primary series is a processed distribution proxy and the EV validation uses reconstructed transactions.
implication_for_direction: The new repository protocol must audit information availability and measured-versus-reconstructed labels for every forecast issue.
